text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The Russian government will on Thursday debate land reform for the first time in eight years.
- Russian fighter jet producer MiG has taken its fight to keep its independence to an arbitration court.
- Former finance minister Alexander Livshits, now an aide to President Boris Yeltsin, has been appointed his representative to the Central Bank.
- Disgruntled workers briefly blocked the Transsiberian railway in Russia's Far East.
- The Duma seems to be reluctant to suspend its holidays and return to Moscow for an extraordinary session.

- Chechnya may lose its main argument -- control over a chunk of an oil pipeline from the Caspian sea to Europe -- in the economic and political tug of war with Moscow, if Russia strikes an oil transportation deal with Georgia.
- A Saudi billionaire is planning to start a bank to finance projects in Chechnya.
- Prosecutors have started criminal proceedings against a dealer in fake computer software.
- Police are conducting in-depth checks at the Sayanogorsk aluminium smelter.
- Moscow stock exchange starts trading in Gazprom shares.
- Russian telecommunications giant Rostelecom is planning to borrow money on the world market to upgrade the domestic telephone network.
SEVODNYA
- A new round of Russian-Chechen negotiations ends with no conclusive deal in sight.
- Moscow traffic police say a dramatic increase in fines has improved the situation on the roads.
- Russian confectionary production has dropped 50 percent since 1990.
- The government has paid its debts to pensioners but new arrears can start accumulating right away.
- Eduard Rossel, governor of the Sverdlovsk region and head of the National Economic Council, gave a cold shoulder to the draft of the new Tax Code.
- Tobacco importers urge the government to lower import duty on Bulgarian cigarettes.
- Rostelecom will raise money by issuing ADRs (American Depositary Receipts) rather than eurobonds.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- The law on restitution of German art which President Yeltsin refuses to sign could drive a wedge between him and the parliament.
- Russian-Chechen negotiations stall over who will be parties to the oil transportation deal.
- President Yeltsin's decree introducing stricter rules for sales of strong alcohol seems to be working.
--Andrei Shukshin, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
